notes.title: 70% Sale! Celebrating 1 month since launch
notes.content:
[h1]Bot Battle Mode is here![/h1]

Thank you to everyone who has played the game so far. The feedback I`ve received is great and people seem to enjoy the game, and that`s the most important thing for me. 

Combat Beans has been live for a month now, and since release I`ve been working through the roadmap as well as taking on board feedback from the community. So to celebrate here`s a 70% sale until Sep 26th.

One of the most common requests was to include a game mode against bots, so that people can jump on and play properly even when nobody is online. Originally, I never planned to add bots (or any major single player mode) to the game, but soon after launch I realised that there are a few hours each day where nobody is online. In those cases, it`s unfair for people who bought the game being unable to experience the game properly. So, I decided to add bots to the game, as well as a new game mode.
You can play against up to 12 bots (I find playing with more bots to be more fun) in a mode where first to get to the kill limit wins the round. Round kill limits can be selected from 10 – 100, and you can also select the difficulty of the bots as well as what weapons they will use. Check out the gameplay below!

[previewyoutube=89cXrO1xiy8;full][/previewyoutube]

As I never did AI before my technical knowledge is quite basic, but I tried to make the bots play like real players as best as I could. They jump and slide around and will melee you if you get too close, though they generally prefer to keep at range if they can. There are still times when they can be a bit derpy, but overall if you`re playing against 12 bots, there`s so much chaos all around that it`s very hard to tell. Over time, I will keep updating the AI behaviour. 

There is one problem I need to fix regarding the Bot Battle Mode, and that is the EXP gained during this mode isn’t being sent back to the playfab servers where all the player data is being stored, because that Bot Battle game mode isn’t being run on an online server on playfab. So, what I need to do is decide to have the EXP and level stored locally on your machine (a bad idea for a number of reasons) or switch to using the steam cloud storage for all the stats. Steam cloud is a much better solution for sure but will take some time for me to set up properly and debug everything. 

Another request I need to take into consideration is to add a feature so that players can host their own public / private sessions. Right now, I`m using playfabs servers to hot games dynamically, where I can easily add or remove servers whenever I need to. In the future, I think it would be great for players to host their own, so I will begin taking a look at the work required to make that happen. 

Over the coming weeks I will keep working through the original planned roadmap, like adding power-ups and team death match, As well as any bug fixing if required. 

Thank you again for playing the game! Please join the discord if you want, and be part of the growing community. 

https://discord.gg/6vcRDyfVzr

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/196915ce21a4ac65d08459c03dc2de8ec5e2ff2c.png[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #6 - Chat, 4.27 update and bug fixes
notes.content:
[b]Devlog #6[/b]

I`ve been busy over the last couple of months working on the game and getting it ready for release. As a public release gets closer, I need to make sure all of the major bugs are fixed and tested. Some of the major bugs and improvements I`ve made are listed below.

[b]•	Update to unreal engine 4.27 [/b]– This is a stop gap before doing a full update to 5.x. Unfortunately, there were a lot of engine errors going straight to 5, so for now I decided to get it updated to 4.27, whilst working on other features for the game. I hope to be able to get the game updated to UE 5 as soon as possible, but I don’t want to risk breaking a ton of other things in the game in the process. As of now the 4.27 build works perfectly fine.

[b]•	Fixes to projectiles,[/b] client and server side – this was a persistent issue in the game from the start. The original system was somewhat simple in its implementation. Arguably too simple. I have now created client side and server side projectiles, which means that the overall feeling of the gunplay is much smoother for clients, regardless of your latency in game. There was also a long running bug where some projectiles wouldn’t multicast their impact hits to all connected clients (which was driving me insane), but this has finally been fixed in the new system.


[b]•	Network improvements[/b] – this isn’t really specific to any one change in the code, but over the last month I`ve been spending a lot of my time identifying where I can reduce network data usage during gameplay. This is important for me as I will be paying for all hosted servers out of my own pocket, so I want the servers to be as optimized as possible. This also will result in better network performance for all players. One of the specific things I`ve been doing is using RepNotify bool variables to trigger events on all clients instead of multicast RPCs. This reduces data usage (for those events) by approximately 80%. 

[b]•	Multiplayer text chat –[/b] a simple thing but required. Players can insult each other’s bean status in-game. Chat can be turned off from the control options sub menu. 

[b]•	Cosmetic asset optimization[/b] – all cosmetics now use soft object references in the game code. That means that the player character wont need load all the assets into memory by default, and will only load the required asset as and when its required. This sounds like a no brainer (and it is, to be fair) but it required a re-work of quite a bit of the logic to make sure the game can handle loading and unloading the assets. The big trade off with soft object references is that you need to manually load and unload those assets from memory, and that can be a pain to get right. 

[b]•	Gameplay balance! [/b]– finally i`ve been able to start doing gameplay tests. Immediately after the test I wrote down a list of things to change and tweak according to the feedback of the testers. One of which is quite apparent in the gameplay video below, and that is the speed of the projectiles. All bullets in the game are actual physical projectiles flying through space, unlike hit scan weapons (like bullets in CS). After thorough play testing, I can safely say the bullet speed right now across the board can be about 2x faster. Also I`ve raised the damage levels of all bullets by about 25 – 30%. This will make gunplay with fast firing machine guns a little more lethal. As of now, explosive weapons like the bazooka, grenade launcher and grenades are definitely the most effective weapons. 

[b]•	“The slime gun is too strong”[/b] – this was funny in the last play test. I dunno, I kind of like having a gun that basically roots you to the ground and stops you from dashing. You know when your screen gets green, you`ll start to scream…

You can see some of the last play test in the video below! 

[previewyoutube=zjltEaOvE5I;full][/previewyoutube]

Leave a comment and let me know what you think of the game play so far. 


In the next update, i`ll be continuing on bug fixes and optimization, reworking some UI elements such as the health bar, and adding a hit scan weapon as a test to see how it plays. I will also begin work on the 4th and 5th maps, and add a few more helmet and dog tag unlocks! Still a lot of work to do, but things are moving forward faster than ever. 
After that, stat tracking is next on the menu.

Come join the discord!

notes.title: Devlog #4 for Combat Beans! - Custom Beans and Unlocks
notes.content:
[h1]Unlocks[/h1]

Welcome to Devlog #4

This week’s topic is showcasing a handful of unlocks.

You gain XP in combat beans by doing all sorts of things. Participating in game rounds, killing players and of course winning rounds. Every time you level up, you`ll unlock some new items to slap on to your bean. 

Currently, these are split into 2 groups. Helmet attachments and the dog tags / neck attachments. 

The helmet attachments fit on top (or somewhere) on the helmet of your bean. They don’t replace the helmet entirely. You still have the ability to change the colours of the helmet underneath the attachment however you like, and combined with a ton of different attachments , you can make some really unique combinations. 

The dog tags are similar, and offer a ton of different colours and visual effects like animated neon glows and funky scanlines. There are also completely custom meshes that replace the dog tags entirely, like the ammo bandoleers, medals (awarded for bravery, of course) and a ton more. 

Along with custom colours , you can mix and match the unlocks to make some unique combos that no other bean would have. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/293920dbddb75bab596566df2e56e7e8ed9a4378.jpg[/img]


So far, everyone thinks the night vision goggles are best (RIP radar ☹ )

[h3]Custom unlocks for participating in community events[/h3]

You want something that LITERALLY no other player would ever have? Well I hope so, because a soon-to-be added feature will allow me to award individual steam IDs with 100% unique unlocks that nobody else would be able to equip, ever. These will be linked to community events, such as art events or best gameplay video. Be sure to hop into the discord to keep up to date with all that jazz. 

The game will launch with plenty to unlock, and more will be added all the time, especially during events. 
Stay tuned for devlog #5!  


Don`t forget to jump into the discord

notes.title: Devlog #3 for Combat Beans! - Maps and UI
notes.content:
[h1]New Maps[/h1]

2 new maps have been added. Both of these have some indoor areas, as well as a variety of floating platforms to get around to some hard-to-reach areas. Here are some screenshots.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_fbdaa929b4f54fc6ada13e57f121bb60~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_a011b994b3d648dcb47ae5c8c25845f1~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_76e23cc1844f4ce4868678725cc5199d~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_d98dba0fb4dc4299970f4a4dd3875986~mv2.jpg[/img]

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_4488300cb76e428fa47b46fd10258ca6~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_c544ba63783d439184a8057f9702c21e~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_b4a470c7916a460fa2e1bdb343d5fcb7~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_4a0be496945b43ad9b19f2f8102797f6~mv2.jpg[/img]


The hardest part of making the maps is the original blocking out of the major shapes and landmarks. It can be easy to spend too much time focusing on one tiny area, only to realize it just doesn’t work out when combined with the rest of the level. A lot of time gets wasted that way, so I split it down into 4 main steps. 

1)	create blocking areas, figuring out where players will be able to run around. 
2)	create line of sight blocking terrain
3)	detailing of landscape height
4)	foliage, props, decals and all other small details.  

Never start with foliage! I wasted too much time re-doing it over and over again. This was because I would make adjustments to the landscape over time, and that caused a lot of foliage to be in the wrong place. procedural foliage can be set up, but the maps here aren’t really ginormous so procedural generation doesn’t particularly save me much time either compared to manually doing it at the end. so always wait until everything else is done first before adding foliage. 

[h1]New ammo counter UI
[/h1]

[b]Old and busted[/b]

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_077857cce7f8422fa62e8e2a5add6abc~mv2.jpg[/img]

[b]New hotness[/b]

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_1ecf1f33406b4120b9693096b11f2425~mv2.jpg[/img]


The new UI now displays an icon showing the weapon that`s equipped, and also the ammo cost per shot. this is important as all guns have different ammo costs when firing, and as I add more guns it`ll be too hard to remember all the costs off by heart. 
Also, the main ammo counter will change to dark grey when you have less ammo than the current cost per shot. this lets you know that even though you have some ammo, you might not have enough to fire the current weapon. 

I`m thinking of switching to a video format for these devlogs from next week. I`ll have to see how much time it takes me and also which format people prefer.
